questions.question: Sandakphu is the highest point in which Indian state?
Sandakphu lies along which ridge?

Sandakphu lies within which national park?

pins.summary: Sandakphu, at about 3,636 meters, is the highest point in West Bengal, located along the Singalila Ridge near the Nepal border. It is famous for offering panoramic views of four of the world's five highest peaks, including Everest, Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, and Makalu, all visible from a single vantage point on clear days. The trek to Sandakphu passes through rhododendron forests that bloom vividly in spring, and Sandakphu lies within the Singalila National Park, which also supports diverse wildlife including the red panda.

questions.question: Namdapha National Park is uniquely known for hosting how many big cat species?
Namdapha National Park is located in which Indian state?

pins.summary: Namdapha National Park, in Arunachal Pradesh's Changlang district, is notable as the only protected area in the world where four big cat species, the tiger, leopard, snow leopard, and clouded leopard, are all found within a single park. Spanning a huge range of elevations from lowland tropical rainforest to high alpine terrain, the park supports an extraordinarily diverse range of ecosystems. It is also home to rare species like the Namdapha flying squirrel, found nowhere else on earth, and due to its remote location, much of the park remains relatively unexplored.

questions.question: Desert National Park is primarily located in which desert?
Desert National Park is a critical habitat for which critically endangered bird?
The Great Indian Bustard's population has declined sharply partly due to collisions with?
Desert National Park is located near which Rajasthan city?

pins.summary: Desert National Park, spread across the Thar Desert near Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, protects one of the largest expanses of desert ecosystem in India, featuring sand dunes, salt lake bottoms, and rocky terrain. It serves as a critical habitat for the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard, one of the heaviest flying birds in the world, whose population has declined sharply due to habitat loss and collisions with power lines. Conservation efforts increasingly focus on protecting the bustard through measures like underground power cabling and captive breeding programs.

pins.summary: Manas National Park, on the border of Assam and Bhutan, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and tiger reserve known for its rich biodiversity, including rare species like the golden langur, pygmy hog, and Bengal florican. The park suffered significant damage during periods of political unrest and poaching in the 1990s, leading UNESCO to briefly place it on its list of World Heritage Sites in danger before conservation efforts helped restore much of its ecological health. Manas is part of a larger transboundary conservation landscape connecting with protected areas in Bhutan.

questions.question: Gir National Park is the last natural habitat of which big cat?
Gir National Park is located in which Indian state?
In the early 20th century, the Asiatic lion population had dropped to roughly how many individuals?
Which pastoral community traditionally lives within the Gir forest?

pins.summary: Gir National Park, in Gujarat, is the last remaining natural habitat of the Asiatic lion, a subspecies once found across much of southwest Asia but now confined almost entirely to this single protected area. Conservation efforts since the early 20th century, when lion numbers had dropped to only a few dozen, have helped the population recover to several hundred individuals today. Gir's dry deciduous forest ecosystem also supports leopards, deer species, and a variety of birdlife, coexisting with several small Maldhari pastoral communities living within the forest.

Who discovered the Bhimbetka Rock Shelters in 1957?

pins.summary: The Bhimbetka Rock Shelters, in Madhya Pradesh, contain some of the earliest known evidence of human life in India, with cave paintings dating back tens of thousands of years, spanning the Mesolithic period through to historical times. The site's more than 700 rock shelters feature paintings depicting hunting scenes, dancing figures, and animals. Discovered by archaeologist V.S. Wakankar in 1957, Bhimbetka is now recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the name is popularly linked to the legendary Mahabharata figure Bhima, though this connection is folklore rather than historical fact.

pins.summary: The Vaishno Devi shrine, located in the Trikuta Hills of Jammu and Kashmir, is one of India's most visited Hindu pilgrimage sites, drawing millions of devotees annually to a cave temple dedicated to the goddess Vaishno Devi. Pilgrims typically undertake a roughly 13-kilometer trek from the base town of Katra to reach the shrine. The shrine's board, established in 1986, has developed extensive infrastructure to accommodate the massive annual pilgrim traffic, and Vaishno Devi is regarded as one of the Shakti Peethas, sites associated with the worship of the divine feminine.

questions.question: The Airavatesvara Temple is located in which town?
Which Chola king built the Airavatesvara Temple?
The Airavatesvara Temple is one of three temples recognized together under which UNESCO listing?

pins.summary: The Airavatesvara Temple, in Darasuram, Tamil Nadu, was built in the 12th century by Chola king Rajaraja II and is one of the three 'Great Living Chola Temples' recognized together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, alongside the Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur and the temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Named after the divine elephant Airavata, believed to have worshipped Shiva at this site, the temple is celebrated for its exceptionally refined stone carvings. A distinctive feature is its front mandapa designed to resemble a chariot with stone wheels, similar in concept to the later Konark Sun Temple.

Bishnupur's temples were built primarily by which dynasty?

pins.summary: Bishnupur, in West Bengal, is renowned for its distinctive terracotta temples built primarily by the Malla dynasty rulers between the 17th and 18th centuries, using locally available clay in the absence of good building stone in the region. The temples feature elaborately carved terracotta panels depicting scenes from Hindu epics, courtly life, and floral motifs. The most famous among them, the Rasmancha, served as a venue for displaying deities during the Ras festival, and Bishnupur is also historically significant as the birthplace of the Bishnupur gharana, a distinct classical music tradition.

pins.summary: Neermahal, in Tripura, is a striking water palace built in the 1930s by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya, situated in the middle of Rudrasagar Lake and accessible only by boat. Combining Hindu and Islamic architectural styles, the palace served as a royal summer retreat, offering the ruling family a secluded escape surrounded by water. Its design, with domes, pavilions, and reflecting pools, drew inspiration from lake palaces elsewhere in India, and today Neermahal hosts an annual water festival featuring boat races and cultural performances.

Salem Steel Plant is a unit of which company?
Salem Steel Plant is located in which Indian state?
In which decade was Salem Steel Plant established?
Salem Steel Plant's specialization reflects SAIL's strategy to serve which type of markets?

pins.summary: Salem Steel Plant, a unit of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) in Tamil Nadu, specializes in producing stainless steel, distinguishing it from most other SAIL plants that primarily manufacture carbon steel. Established in the 1980s, the plant supplies stainless steel sheets and coils used in industries ranging from kitchenware and architecture to automotive and industrial equipment manufacturing. Salem Steel Plant's specialization reflects SAIL's broader diversification strategy to serve niche, higher-value steel product markets alongside its core bulk steel operations.

questions.question: IFFCO's Phulpur plant is located in which state?
IFFCO stands for which type of organization?
IFFCO's ownership structure is unique because it is owned by?
The Phulpur plant primarily manufactures which fertilizer product?
IFFCO's model aims to make fertilizer more accessible for?

pins.summary: IFFCO's Phulpur plant, in Uttar Pradesh, is one of the flagship facilities of the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative (IFFCO), a cooperative society structure unique among major Indian fertilizer producers, owned collectively by farmer cooperative societies rather than the government or private shareholders. Established in the 1970s, the plant primarily manufactures urea, a key input supporting India's Green Revolution-era and subsequent agricultural productivity gains. IFFCO's cooperative model has made it one of the world's largest fertilizer cooperatives, aiming to keep fertilizer more accessible for member farmers.

questions.question: The Nangal Fertilizer Plant is located in which state?
Nangal Fertilizer Plant benefited from proximity to which hydroelectric project?
Nangal Fertilizer Plant played a key role in supporting which agricultural transformation?
In which decade was the Nangal Fertilizer Plant established?
Nangal's fertilizer production primarily focuses on which type of fertilizer?

pins.summary: The Nangal Fertilizer Plant, in Punjab, was established in the 1960s as part of India's early push toward chemical fertilizer self-sufficiency, benefiting from its proximity to the Bhakra Nangal hydroelectric project's abundant power supply. The plant played an important role in supporting Punjab's transformation into a leading agricultural state during the Green Revolution, supplying nitrogenous fertilizers to farmers across the region. Nangal's development was closely tied to the broader industrial complex built around the Bhakra Dam, reflecting a period of Indian planning that linked hydropower with downstream industry.

questions.question: The Khetri Copper Complex is located in which state?
Khetri Copper Complex primarily produces which metal?
Khetri Copper Complex operates under which company?
Khetri's copper mining history dates back how far?
Khetri Copper Complex was developed mainly to reduce India's dependence on?

pins.summary: The Khetri Copper Complex, in Rajasthan, is one of India's major copper mining and smelting operations, developed from the 1960s onward to reduce the country's dependence on imported copper. The region around Khetri has a long history of copper mining dating back centuries, with ancient workings later expanded through modern industrial mining techniques under Hindustan Copper Limited. Khetri's copper deposits are considered significant not just for volume but also for historical continuity, representing one of India's oldest continuously exploited metal resources alongside sites like Zawar's zinc mines.

pins.summary: Kolar Gold Fields, in Karnataka, was once among the deepest gold mines in the world, with shafts extending more than three kilometers underground before mining operations ceased in the early 2000s due to declining ore grades and rising costs. The mines operated for over a century, starting under British colonial management in the late 19th century before being nationalized after independence. Kolar's mining township developed unique infrastructure historically, including one of India's earliest hydroelectric power supplies specifically built to support the mining operations.

pins.summary: Gangaur is a major festival celebrated across Rajasthan, with particularly grand processions in Udaipur, dedicated to the goddess Gauri, symbolizing marital harmony and celebrated by both married and unmarried women. The festival features elaborately dressed idols of Gauri and Shiva (as Isar) carried in colorful processions through city streets, accompanied by traditional folk songs and dances. In Udaipur, the procession often moves toward the city's lake, with boats carrying the idols across the water in a particularly picturesque tradition unique to the city.

pins.summary: Ugadi marks the traditional New Year for Telugu and Kannada-speaking communities, celebrated widely across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana including in Vijayawada, typically falling in March or April according to the lunisolar calendar. A central ritual involves eating 'ugadi pachadi,' a dish combining sweet, sour, bitter, salty, and spicy flavors symbolizing the varied emotions life brings throughout the coming year. Homes are decorated with mango leaf garlands, and Panchanga Sravanam, a ritual reading of astrological predictions for the new year, is also a significant part of the celebrations.

questions.question: Yaoshang is celebrated in which Indian state, around the same time as Holi?
What is the moonlit group dance associated with Yaoshang called?
Yaoshang blends indigenous Meitei customs with which later religious influence?

pins.summary: Yaoshang, celebrated in Manipur around the same time as Holi, is a traditional festival combining indigenous Meitei customs with Vaishnavite influences introduced centuries ago, marked by five days of communal celebration in Imphal and across the state. A distinctive feature is 'Thabal Chongba,' a moonlit group dance in which young men and women dance together in circles. Children traditionally go door to door collecting small donations, a practice known as 'Nakadeng,' reflecting Manipur's blend of older indigenous traditions with later religious and cultural influences.

questions.question: Bathukamma is a festival primarily celebrated by women in which Indian state?
Bathukamma involves arranging seasonal flowers into what shape?
How many days does the Bathukamma festival typically span?
"Bathukamma" roughly translates to which phrase?
Bathukamma gained special prominence as a symbol of Telangana's identity after which event?

pins.summary: Bathukamma is a floral festival celebrated primarily by women in Telangana, including in Warangal, involving the arrangement of colorful seasonal flowers in a conical stack that is later immersed in water, accompanied by traditional songs and circular dances. The festival, spanning nine days, coincides with the flowering season following the monsoon and is deeply tied to Telangana's regional cultural identity, particularly gaining prominence as a symbol of the state's distinct heritage after Telangana's formation in 2014. 'Bathukamma' translates roughly to 'Mother Goddess, come alive.'

pins.summary: The Reh Festival, celebrated by the Idu Mishmi tribe in and around Roing, Arunachal Pradesh, is an important cultural and religious festival marked by rituals aimed at seeking protection from evil spirits and ensuring prosperity for the coming year. The festival involves the sacrifice of animals as offerings, traditional songs and dances performed in elaborate tribal attire, and community feasting that brings together Idu Mishmi families from surrounding villages. Reh reflects the animist spiritual traditions of the Idu Mishmi, one of Arunachal Pradesh's many distinct tribal communities.

pins.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), headquartered in New Delhi, is India's premier federal investigative agency, handling cases involving corruption, major economic offenses, and serious or sensitive crimes that often cross state jurisdictions. Established in 1963, the CBI's origins trace back to the Special Police Establishment, initially set up during World War II. Unlike state police forces, the CBI typically requires either a court order, a state government's consent, or a central government directive to investigate cases, and it has periodically faced criticism over questions of political independence.

The CAG's independence from executive control is considered essential for?

pins.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), headquartered in New Delhi, is a constitutional authority responsible for auditing the accounts and expenditures of both the central government and state governments. Established under the Constitution, the CAG's reports are submitted to the President or state governors and subsequently tabled in the relevant legislatures, forming the basis for scrutiny by Public Accounts Committees. Several high-profile CAG reports have brought major cases of alleged financial irregularity into public and political debate, and its independence from executive control is considered essential to public financial accountability.

pins.summary: Imphal, the capital of Manipur, is tied to a distinctive constitutional arrangement under Article 371C, which provides special provisions for the state's hill areas, requiring a dedicated committee of the state legislature to address the specific administrative needs of these predominantly tribal regions. Manipur's political integration into India followed its 1949 merger agreement, a process that remains a subject of historical debate. The state achieved full statehood in 1972, having earlier existed as a Union Territory, and Manipur's diverse ethnic composition, including Meitei, Naga, and Kuki-Zo communities, has continued to shape its political arrangements.

questions.question: Tripura's merger with India took place in which year?

pins.summary: Agartala, the capital of Tripura, is closely tied to the former princely state's merger with India in October 1949, following the death of its last reigning monarch. Tripura initially became a Part C state and later a Union Territory before being granted full statehood in 1972, alongside Manipur and Meghalaya. The state's demographic composition shifted dramatically following large-scale migration after Partition, altering the balance between indigenous tribal populations and Bengali-speaking settlers, and tribal governance is now supported through the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council.

questions.question: Arunachal Pradesh achieved full statehood in which year?

Arunachal Pradesh first became a Union Territory in which year?
Arunachal Pradesh's border disputes are primarily with which country?
China refers to parts of Arunachal Pradesh by which disputed name?

pins.summary: Itanagar, the capital of Arunachal Pradesh, oversees a state that achieved full statehood only in 1987, having previously been administered as the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) directly under central government control due to its strategic sensitivity along the disputed border with China. Arunachal Pradesh first became a Union Territory in 1972 before its transition to full statehood fifteen years later. The state is home to more than twenty major tribal communities, and its border location has continued to give it strategic significance, including recurring territorial disputes with China.
